perspective:
Alice Lim’s available information:

- She knows she is a dental hygienist and that Austin is an old friend from high school; they are close and discuss their personal/professional lives.
- She knows Austin works in an office setting/insurance context, and that his career path differs from hers.
- She notices Austin has been reserved lately when work comes up. She suspects/believes he may be hiding something about his job performance. She feels concerned and curious, so she invites him to coffee.
- She asks Austin if everything is okay at the office and says he can talk to her. She hears him say it’s “nothing really,” just “usual ups and downs,” and that he’s “not sure how to handle a few things at work” and that it’s “complicated.”
- From this, she believes Austin may be considering a career change because of dissatisfaction at work. She feels worried for him and shares her own healthcare experiences, suggesting healthcare as a possible path.
- She hears Austin say he has thought about changing careers but doesn’t know what other paths to take; he asks what she suggests and says he’d like to know more about her experiences.
- She senses Austin is hesitant because of fear of the unknown. She feels frustration and empathy, then tells him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and is happier.
- She hears Austin say that Lara’s story is inspiring but that he worries about risks and the initial struggle. She tells him growth comes from leaving comfort zones and that she supports him. He thanks her and says her support and real success stories help.
- She sees Austin is open to the discussion, feels encouraged and hopeful, and offers to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. She hears him appreciate the connections. She says she’ll set up a meeting next week; he says he’s looking forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings she participated in, she believes Austin is ready to take next steps and appreciates her help. She feels satisfaction and joy. She tells him she’s proud of his steps; he says he feels excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful. She proposes regular check-ins; he agrees, saying it will keep him focused and that her perspective is good.
- She does not have direct confirmation of Austin’s actual job performance, hidden motives, or private feelings beyond what he stated; she has only her observations, suspicions, and his statements to her.
